title: Genuine cross-frequency coupling networks in human resting-state electrophysiological recordings (Siebenhuehner et al., 2020): SEEG and MEG connectomes (derivative)
description: This derivative dataset provides per-subject resting-state connectivity matrices computed from stereo-EEG (59 epilepsy patients) and MEG (19 healthy participants plus a 10-participant eyes-open/eyes-closed cohort). Measures include phase synchrony (PLV, wPLI), cross-frequency phase synchrony, phase-amplitude coupling and amplitude-envelope coupling, each with surrogate values, mapped to Destrieux-atlas parcels. Supporting files, neuropsychological scores and plotted figure values from the original Dryad release are repackaged in BIDS form. Raw recordings are not included.
methods_description: Ten-minute eyes-closed resting-state SEEG was recorded at 1000 Hz with closest-white-matter referencing. Ten-minute eyes-open resting-state MEG was recorded on a 306-channel Elekta/MEGIN system, processed with tSSS and ICA, and source-modelled with MNE onto 200 parcels with fidelity weighting. Morlet wavelet filter banks (m=5) covering about 1.1-315 Hz were used to compute synchrony and cross-frequency coupling matrices with surrogates.
